title: Needs Remediation
description: Reference project preserving the original baseline → exploration → converged direction model for a saved operational view.
reviewQuestions: Does the selected direction distinguish a fixed saved-view definition from user-controlled narrowing filters?
Does the task-first toolbar preserve the production table while making the operational goal clearer?

versions.name: Baseline
versions.whatChanged: No design change. Preserves the trusted production starting point.
versions.question: What does the existing production view already establish that must not regress?
versions.decisionRationale: Retained as the accepted starting reference for later comparisons.

versions.name: Definition outside
versions.whatChanged: Moved the fixed saved-view definition outside the filter model.
versions.question: Would separating the definition from filters clarify what the user can and cannot change?
versions.decisionRationale: Useful structural exploration, but weaker than the task-first direction at expressing the operational job.

versions.name: Task-first toolbar
versions.whatChanged: Made the task and narrowing controls the dominant toolbar model.
versions.question: Does a task-first toolbar better explain the view while preserving user-controlled narrowing?
versions.decisionRationale: Kept as the strongest alternative because it exposed the core task without redesigning the underlying table.

versions.name: HiFi task-first
versions.whatChanged: Refined the task-first exploration into the current high-fidelity direction while preserving the production table.
versions.question: Can the task-first model converge into a product-fidelity direction without losing the trusted baseline?
versions.decisionRationale: Selected because it best separates fixed view meaning from user-controlled filters and preserves established table behaviour.

decisionLog.decision: Keep one stable view name across navigation, breadcrumb and page context.
decisionLog.rationale: Competing names made the object model harder to understand.

decisionLog.decision: Treat the saved-view definition as explanatory copy, not removable filter chips.
decisionLog.rationale: The definition describes the fixed scope of the view; user filters only narrow within it.

decisionLog.decision: Preserve the existing message table behaviour.
decisionLog.rationale: The design question concerns the header/filter model, not a redesign of the underlying table.

decisionLog.decision: Do not converge on the definition-outside exploration.
decisionLog.rationale: It clarified the fixed definition, but it did not express the operational task as strongly as the task-first model.

context.problem: A saved operational view has a fixed definition, but the existing filter presentation can make that definition look removable or user-controlled.
context.intendedOutcome: Explain the fixed scope of the view while letting users confidently narrow results with their own filters.
users: Security operations users reviewing messages requiring remediation
context.workflow: Users open a stable Needs Remediation view, understand its fixed definition, then narrow within it using operational filters while preserving the existing table workflow.
context.currentDirection: A task-first header and toolbar that states the job clearly, separates the fixed view definition from user-controlled narrowing and leaves the production table intact.
constraints: Preserve the trusted production table and row behaviour.
Use one stable name for the view.
Do not represent fixed definition terms as removable filter chips.
acceptedDecisions: Use the task-first toolbar as the current direction.
Keep the fixed definition separate from user-controlled filters.
openQuestions: How much explanatory copy is needed before the fixed definition becomes visually heavy?
Which parts of the task-first model should become reusable product patterns?
